title: Tech Mahindra and Uniphore Partner to Build Agentic AI Factory for Enterprise Clients
excerpt: The Indian IT giant and Palo Alto-based AI firm will jointly develop and deploy autonomous AI agents for retail and financial services, starting with procurement and claims processing workflows.
body:
• Tech Mahindra and Uniphore have partnered to co-build an Agentic AI Factory that will develop, deploy, and manage autonomous AI agents for enterprise clients globally.
  • The initial focus targets retail strategic sourcing and BFSI claims processing, with plans to expand to additional industries and regions.
  • The factory will integrate Uniphore's Business AI Cloud platform with Tech Mahindra's digital transformation expertise across 90 countries and 1,100+ clients.
  • The partnership aims to help enterprises move beyond generic AI chatbots to domain-specific, outcome-driven agentic systems.

Tech Mahindra and Uniphore announced a partnership this week to co-build and deliver agentic AI solutions for enterprise clients worldwide, combining the Indian IT services giant's global delivery capabilities with the Palo Alto-based AI company's cloud platform.

The collaboration establishes what the companies call an Agentic AI Factory — a dedicated operation to develop, deploy, and manage purpose-built small-language models, AI agents, and industry-specific solutions. Tech Mahindra will integrate Uniphore's Business AI Cloud (BAIC) platform, which is designed to unify enterprise data, knowledge, and AI agents with built-in security and governance.

From Chatbots to Autonomous Agents

The partnership reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI from experimental chatbot deployments toward systems capable of reasoning, planning, and autonomously executing multi-step tasks. Where earlier AI tools required constant human oversight, agentic AI aims to handle complex workflows end-to-end — a step change that enterprises have struggled to implement at scale.

"Enterprises are increasingly looking to move beyond generic AI to solutions that are deeply contextual, domain-aware, and outcome-driven."

— Birendra Sen, President, Business Process Services, Tech Mahindra

Sen added that the partnership would enable clients to "accelerate AI adoption with precision, unlocking tangible business value across key sectors like BFSI and Retail."

Retail and Financial Services First

The initial deployment targets two high-priority domains. In retail, the companies will co-develop solutions for strategic sourcing, applying agentic AI to procurement workflows, supplier intelligence, and cost optimization. In banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI), the first solutions will address unclaimed benefits and claims processing — areas where accuracy, regulatory compliance, and speed of resolution are critical.

Carl Borsody, Uniphore's chief revenue officer, framed the collaboration as a way to turn a technology platform into a repeatable delivery model. "Tech Mahindra brings domain expertise across 90 countries and 1,100+ global clients," he said. "Together, we are combining Tech Mahindra's expertise with our Business AI Cloud that brings the sovereign, composable foundation to extend an Agentic AI Factory into a repeatable delivery motion."

A Busy Stretch for Tech Mahindra's AI Push

The Uniphore partnership arrives during an active period for Tech Mahindra's AI and digital transformation business. Earlier this week, Vodafone Business announced a collaboration with the company to deliver technology services to UK enterprise customers, drawing on capabilities including AI-led transformation, private 5G, IoT, and cloud infrastructure. Last week, Tech Mahindra and ServiceNow expanded a multi-year partnership to help enterprises scale AI deployments from pilot to production, with plans to establish an AI and Innovation Centre of Excellence.

Tech Mahindra, part of the Mahindra Group founded in 1945, employs more than 146,000 professionals globally. The company has been positioning itself at the intersection of IT services and AI, seeking to capture demand from enterprises that want AI integrated into existing business processes rather than deployed as standalone tools.

What It Means for Indian IT

The deal underscores a strategic pivot for India's IT services sector. As traditional outsourcing contracts face pricing pressure and automation erodes lower-value work, companies like Tech Mahindra are betting that AI-native service delivery — where agents handle tasks that once required large teams — will define the next wave of growth. Uniphore, founded by Umesh Sachdev and Ravi Saraogi, is itself a product of India's AI ecosystem, having grown from a Bangalore startup into a platform trusted by more than 2,000 large enterprises globally, according to the company.

While the initial focus spans retail and BFSI, the Agentic AI Factory model is designed to extend to additional industries and geographies in the coming months, the companies said.
